Evaluating a release rule from the released alone

Source: R/corr.R
sellab.Rd

Failures (a missed court date, a new arrest) are seen only for the defendants a judge released. A proposed rule that releases only people the judge released is scored exactly from their outcomes; one that releases people the judge detained has a failure rate known only up to the worst and best cases for them, an interval whose width is the share of the rule's releases the judge detained. Both ends can occur. The naive score on the rule's observed releases alone always lies inside the interval, but reports one point of it as if it were known. See proof("sellab").

Usage

sellab(y, rel, rule, w = NULL)

Arguments

y

Failures: 1 or 0 for each released defendant; values for detained defendants are ignored and may be NA.

rel

Released by the judge: TRUE or FALSE for each defendant. When y, rel, rule (and w) are all named with unique names, they are matched by name; otherwise by position.

rule

Released by the rule: TRUE or FALSE, same length.

w

NULL for equal weights, or one non-negative weight per defendant.

Value

A named numeric vector: obs (the failure rate among the judge's releases), unobs (the share of the rule's releases the judge detained), lower and upper (the bounds on the rule's failure rate), width (upper - lower, equal to unobs) and naive (the failure rate on the rule's releases that were observed; NaN when none were).

References

Lakkaraju, H., Kleinberg, J., Leskovec, J., Ludwig, J. and Mullainathan, S. (2017). The selective labels problem. Proceedings of the 23rd ACM SIGKDD International Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining, 275-284. doi:10.1145/3097983.3098066

Examples

set.seed(4)
risk <- runif(500)
y <- rbinom(500, 1, risk)
sellab(y, rel = risk < 0.7, rule = risk < 0.8)
#>       obs     unobs     lower     upper     width     naive 
#> 0.3488372 0.1202046 0.3069054 0.4271100 0.1202046 0.3488372
